newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: CRICKET-STEWART EYES 100 AS RAIN HALTS PLAY IN NZ. [CORRECTED 5:51 GMT]
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-STEWART EYES 100 AS RAIN HALTS PLAY IN NZ. [CORRECTED 5:51 GMT]

text.p: Alec Stewart's plans for a century were interrupted on Tuesday when heavy rain forced play to be abandoned on day two of England's four-day cricket tour match against a New Zealand Selection XI.
The tourists were 154-3 (corrects) in reply to the New Zealand side's 138 all out when play was called off for the day at lunch.
Stewart, the world's top run scorer in tests in 1996, added a fluent 35 to advance his overnight score to 75 not out as England took a convincing first innings lead.
He displayed tidy defence and punished anything loose to move to his 50 with fours in consecutive balls from medium pacer Justin Vaughan.
It had taken him 94 balls and included seven boundaries.
That over produced 11 runs, and when fast-medium Danny Morrison came on for the seventh over of the day, he twice dropped the ball short and Stewart hooked and pulled him to the fence.

Hussain had a tentative start, edging Vaughan just short of Craig Spearman at second slip before he had scored in the second over of the day. He got moving by cutting the next ball to the backward point boundary.

Only 14.3 overs were bowled before rain, thunder and lightning washed out the rest of the day. England, starting the day at 106-3, had added 48 (corrects) runs without further loss and Hussain was unbeaten on 11.
